headline: Florida owned Saturday because Jadan Baugh made FAU chase the run, and Aaron Philo took the throw FAU kept leaving. The areas of opportunity were the easy throw and the calls in the secondary. Florida’s corners lined up seven yards off the receiver, and the back end wasn’t getting the same call. FAU caught it in front of them all night. That’s why the defense ran 90 plays.

offense.body:
Faulkner’s plan: make FAU wrong about the crease without changing the start of the play.

Same run look. Three different answers.

If FAU played it straight: Baugh hit it or cut it back — 14 for 160 and three scores. The cutback is who he is.

If FAU sat downhill: Faulkner changed the lead. Third-and-2, tight end seals, tackle wraps, Baugh follows it 61 yards.

If FAU stayed back: Philo took the short throw. When they softened even more, he went over the top — Abrams for 63, Stockton walking in from 12.

The motion before the snap was the tell. A receiver walked across. If a defender ran with him, it was man. If he stayed, it was zone. Same start. Different answer.

Baugh got the space because the plan is built for him. First-down chains. Explosives when FAU guessed wrong.

Brown’s 49 was a short throw that he took the rest of the way. Abrams’ 63 was the deep ball when the safety stayed too far back. Baugh’s 61 was the edge when they sat on the crease.

Philo ran the operation. First drive, he worked through the read and found Wilson for 19. When he threw on time, the plan was easy. When he held it, the play died. The interception was off Mays’ hands — Sweeney sitting underneath.

The line was clean — one false start, no late-shift disaster. They climbed on the run that won the night. The mistake that loses real games was the snap over Philo’s head inside the 5 — twenty yards lost.

defense.body:
White’s plan: keep help over the top, rush four, take away the deep ball, live with the short one if you tackle it.

Four down. Extra defensive back. Woods on the edge. The disguise was linebackers walking up, then dropping — baiting throws into coverage.

The throw that stayed open was the short one. FAU never huddled. They took the five-to-eight yard catch all night. Corners seven yards off and bailing — that’s ninety plays. Sumrall said it: third-and-1, your corner cannot be nine yards off.

The jobs that failed: the cushion, the calls in the secondary, and the edge when the quarterback kept it. When the outside defender left, Veltkamp walked in from the 7. At the 1, they had numbers and still lost the yard.

The jobs that hit: Chiles and Coleman blowing up the throw-it-now screens. Coleman baiting the first pick. Coleman tipping the next one. Johnson catching it. Bett beating the quarterback at the 1. McCloud winning fourth-and-2. The rush pushing the pocket even if the ball was out fast.

The structure killed the shot over the top. It allowed volume. Ninety plays. A 20-yard fade to Valsin.

The fix: force the throw over you. Get the same call in the secondary. Set the edge when the quarterback runs.

Jobs that hit: Coleman’s pick, Coleman’s tip to Johnson, Bett at the 1, McCloud on fourth-and-2.

specials.body: Durkin from 53 — three points from a stalled drive. No punts. FAU’s 18-yard punt set up Stockton’s score. Specials flipped the field once and didn’t give any back.

Defense: help over the top, rush four, live with the short throw only if the back end is on the same page.
